zh: 都柏林大学学院是爱尔兰国立大学的成员分校之一. 爱尔兰都柏林的一所公立研究型大学，是爱尔兰国立大学的成员机构. 拥有38,417名学生，是爱尔兰最大的大学，也是欧洲最负盛名的大学之一. UCD的现任和前任教职员工和校友中有五位诺贝尔奖获得者. 并且，四位爱尔兰总理和三位爱尔兰总统以及一位印度总统也是UCD的毕业生.

UCD起源于1854年成立的一个组织，于圣马拉基节以约翰·亨利·纽曼为首任校长成立了爱尔兰天主教大学；它于1880年再次重组并于1908年获得特许状. 1997年的《大学法案》将该成员大学更名为「爱尔兰国立大学都柏林分校」，而1998年的部长令将该机构更名为「都柏林国立大学学院-爱尔兰国立大学都柏林分校」. 最初位于都柏林市中心的圣斯蒂芬绿地和厄尔斯福特大道，所有学院已迁至位于离市中心南部六公里处的贝尔菲尔德占地133公顷（330英亩）的校园. 1991年，UCD购买了位于布莱克罗克的第二个场地. 目前该地是迈克尔·斯穆里特研究生商学院的所在地，是爱尔兰最好的商学院之一.
EIRSAT-1（Educational Irish Research Satellite-1）是由爱尔兰都柏林的都柏林大学（UCD）开发和建造的欧洲太空总署赞助的2U立方卫星，2023年12月1日，EIRSAT-1在加利福尼亚州范登堡太空军基地搭载猎鹰9号火箭发射升空. 到达轨道后，它成为爱尔兰的第一颗卫星.
2015年5月发布的一份报告显示，UCD及其学生在爱尔兰创造的经济产出每年达到13亿欧元.

都柏林大学的历史可追溯到成立于1851年的爱尔兰天主教大学. 该校位于都柏林市中心的圣史蒂芬绿地大街86号，首任校长为著名的教育家真福者约翰·亨利·纽曼，爱尔兰著名作家詹姆斯·乔伊斯曾就读于该校. 1908年爱尔兰天主教大学与科克女王学院和高威女王学院合并成立了爱尔兰国立大学，原爱尔兰天主教大学因此改名为都柏林大学学院. 1934年买下了贝尔菲尔德(Belfield)，1960年在爱尔兰政府的建议下，都柏林大学从原来的市中心迁址至位于都柏林市郊的占地300公顷的贝尔菲尔德校园，根据1997年大学法案成为一个自治学院.
en: University College Dublin, commonly referred to as UCD, is a public research university in Dublin, Ireland, and a member institution of the National University of Ireland. With more than 38,000 students, it is Ireland's largest university.

UCD originates in a body founded in 1854, which opened as the Catholic University of Ireland on the feast of St. Malachy with John Henry Newman as its first rector; it re-formed in 1880 and chartered in its own right in 1908. The Universities Act, 1997 renamed the constituent university as the "National University of Ireland, Dublin", and a ministerial order of 1998 renamed the institution as "University College Dublin – National University of Ireland, Dublin".

Originally located at St Stephen's Green and Earlsfort terrace in Dublin's city centre, all faculties later relocated to a 133 ha campus at Belfield, six kilometres to the south of the city centre. In 1991, it purchased a second site in Blackrock, which currently houses the Michael Smurfit Graduate Business School. A report published in May 2015 asserted that the economic output generated by UCD and its students in Ireland amounted to €1.3 billion annually.

UCD can trace its history to the institution founded in 1854 as the Catholic University of Ireland. Renamed University College in 1883 and put under the control of the Jesuits in 1883, it became University College Dublin in 1908, a constituent college of the National University of Ireland under the Universities Act.

After the Catholic Emancipation period of Irish history, Archbishop of Armagh attempted to provide, for the first time in Ireland, higher-level education for followers of the Catholic Church and taught by such people. The Catholic hierarchy demanded a Catholic alternative to the University of Dublin's Trinity College, whose Anglican origins the hierarchy refused to overlook. Since the 1780s, the University of Dublin had admitted Catholics to study; a religious test, however, hindered the efforts of Catholics in their desire to obtain membership in the university's governing bodies. Thus, in 1850 at the Synod of Thurles, it was decided to open a university in Dublin for Catholics.
